findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple areas in the physical facility needing repair:
1) SECOND REPEAT: Under the left side of the sink at the dish machine there are multiple tiles that have come loose from the wall.
2) SECOND REPEAT: The bar hand-sink needs sealed to the wall. Facilities that cannot be moved for cleaning should be adhered to the wall to prevent the entry and harborage of mold.
3) FIRST REPEAT There are tiles underneath the dry storage along the north wall of the kitchen have separated from the wall.
Ensure repairs are made by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Inspector observed shrimp being thawed in the basin of the hand washing sink next to the kitchen office. CORRECTED- shrimp was removed from the sink. Ensure hand washing sinks are used for no other purpose than hand washing, so as to not deter hand washing.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. [Pf]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple areas in the facility needing repair:
1) FIRST REPEAT: Under the left side of the sink at the dish machine there are multiple tiles that have come loose from the wall.
2) FIRST REPEAT: The bar hand-sink needs caulked to the wall. Facilities that cannot be moved for cleaning should be adhered to the wall to be made smooth and easily cleanable.
3) There are tiles underneath the dry storage along the north wall of the kitchen have separated from the wall.
Ensure repairs are made by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
FIRST REPEAT: None of the facility’s Certified Food Protection Managers (CFPM)s have allergen awareness certificates. Allergen Awareness information (given during the previous inspection) is in black binder with the other paperwork. Certified Food Protection Managers are required to obtain allergen awareness training in Class I facilities. Certificates must be renewed every 3 years.

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.[C]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the basin of the  handwashing sink at the facility’s bar to be obstructed by a container of Clorox wipes. CORRECTED- the wipes were removed. Ensure handwashing sinks are made available for handwashing only at all times.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.[Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
Multiple food contact surfaces were found to contain an accumulation of soil debris:
1) Back of the ice baffles in the large server prep room.
2) Soda nozzles of the bar server station.
CORRECTED- the ice machine was emptied and wiped with a clean sanitizer rag. The soda nozzles were removed to be cleaned, brushed, and sanitized.
Ensure food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of soil debris. This frequency may need to increase with use and variable outdoor temperatures.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiples areas in the facility needing repair:
1) Under the left side of the sink at the dish machine there are multiple tiles that have come loose from the wall.
2) The walls on either side of the mop sink contain exposed wood. Ensure the walls are covered with a smooth, easily cleanable surface to prevent the harborage of mold. 
3) The bar hand-sink needs caulked to the wall. Facilities that cannot be moved for cleaning should be adhered to the wall to be made smooth and easily cleanable.
Ensure repairs are made by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
None of the facility’s CFMs have allergen awareness certificates. Discussion was had between inspector and PIC, and inspector gave the PIC a list of accredited institutes for allergen awareness training. Certified Food Protection Managers are required to obtain allergen awareness training. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.[C]

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: The manager’s Certified Food Protection Manager’s certificate recently expired and they have not retaken the test yet. Ensure that there is always a CFPM on site during all hours of operation. The PIC stated that he will be taking it soon and did not realize that it had expired.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: The dish shelves were observed to be in need of cleaning. Ensure that these are cleaned and maintained cleaned.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: There is a piece of wall trim that is in disrepair to the right of the triple sink. Ensure that this is repaired and maintained in good repair.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: There was raw meat observed to be stored above potatoes and rolls in the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED- The raw meat was moved from above these items and staff was educated on storage order. Ensure that food is protected from cross contamination during storage and holding. 

 (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P).

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.comment:
5-205.15: There was a leak observed in the triple sink faucet. Ensure that this leak is repaired by next routine inspection. Plumbing systems should be maintained in good repair. 

A PLUMBING SYSTEM shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Conveyor belt dish machine final rinse observed reaching less than 160F, according to the a heat-sensing sticker and inspector’s plate thermometer. PIC restarted the booster, at which time the machine reached at least 160F on the heat sensing sticker and 180F on the machine’s built-in baffle thermometer.
4-501.112: (A) Temperature of the fresh hot water SANITIZING rinse may not be more than 194F or less than 160F for stationary rack, single temperature machines. All other machines can be no less than 180F. (B) Maximum temperature does not apply to high pressure and temperature systems with wand-type spraying devices. [P]

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: No ambient thermometer is present in the 2 door cooler near the back door. CORRECTED- A thermometer was moved from the out-of-use salad bowl cooler. Ensure thermometers are present in all cold holding equipment. (Previously observed 10/25/2023.)
4-204.112: (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. [C]

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
There is a gap along the bottom of the windowed back door where daylight is visible when the door is shut. Add a sweep or otherwise close the gap so that the door is tight-fitting and protected against pests.
6-202.15: (A) Outer openings of FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against entry of insects and rodents. (B) Does not apply to FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS which opens into larger structure. (C) Exterior doors need not be self-closing if designed for limited-use. (D) If opening present, opening shall be protected against rodent and insects. (E) Paragraph (D) not applicable when pests are absent. [C]

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
Facility does not have a vomit/diarrhea clean up policy on file. CORRECTED- Inspector emailed a clean up policy to be printed and kept on site in case norovirus disinfection is needed.
2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Sanitizer bucket near the salad prep area observed with 100 ppm quat sanitizer. CORRECTED- PIC remade sanitizer bucket to 200ppm quat.
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have a concentration based on the label (200-400ppm). [P]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
-Heavy cream observed in the bar cooler without any date-marking. CORRECTED- Un-dated heavy cream was voluntarily discarded.
-Orange juice in the bar cooler observed with a written date mark of 10/20, and a manufacturer use by date of 10/19. CORRECTED- Orange juice was voluntarily discarded.
-BP glaze in the walk-in cooler observed with a date marking of 10/15. CORRECTED- Glaze was voluntarily discarded.
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1. (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date. (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food. (D) Approved date marking systems. (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container. (F) Does not apply to shellstock.  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma). [Pf]

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
No ambient thermometer is present in the 2 door cooler near the back door. Ensure thermometers are present in all cold holding equipment.
4-204.112: (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. [C]

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
At least one employee working this evening does not have a food handler certificate on file. Ensure all food employees have current food handler certificates on file.
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement. [C]

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
PIC does not have an allergen training certificate on file. Other allergen training certificates on file have expired. Ensure all CFMs complete allergen training. Keep certificates on file for review during inspections.
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Conveyor belt dish machine final rinse observed reaching temperatures in excess of 194F, according to the built-in thermometer. DishTemp plate thermometers indicated a plate temp of 152-154F after multiple runs through the machine. Service machine. Use an additional sanitize step until machine is functioning properly. 
4-501.112: (A) Temperature of the fresh hot water SANITIZING rinse may not be more than 194F or less than 165F for stationary rack, single temperature machines. All other machines can be no less than 180F. (B) Maximum temperature does not apply to high pressure and temperature systems with wand-type spraying devices.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11 Can opener blade was soiled with stuck on debris and was not used to open anything during prep for the current operating day. Kitchen manager took the can opener to the dish area to be cleaned and sanitized. 
Food contact surfaces shall be clean to sight and touch. Properly clean and sanitize food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils between uses.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 Mold was observed on the baffle in the ice machine bin. Kitchen manager noted inside the ice machine bin was just cleaned about 2 weeks ago. Ensure cleaning occurs as needed to eliminate buildup. 
Equipment such as ice bins and enclosed components shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.18 (A) Heavy whipping cream in the bar cooler had a date mark of 9/8 and was past the seven day time frame for use. Whipping cream was discarded. Ensure date marked foods are used or discarded within seven days. Discard products at the close of business on the 7th day to ensure compliance. 
A food specified in  3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in  3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or package that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in  3501.17(A).

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.12 1. Scoop used for whole coffee beans was on top of the coffee maker where some dust accumulation was observed. Scoop was removed for cleaning and storage in a clean container was discussed.
2. Ice scoop holder at south server area was observed with a small piece of debris in the bottom. Holder and scoop were removed for cleaning. 
3. Ice scoop holders attached to soda machine at the bar and the ice bin in the bar had some dust accumulation on inner surfaces. Ensure cleaning of holders as needed to eliminate accumulation of dust. 
During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food preparation and dispensing utensils shall be stored in clean, protected location if utensils, such as ice scoops, are used only with non-TCS food.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 Floor and lower wall were soiled with splash and general buildup of debris between the dirty dish counter and dish machine. Cleaning frequency was discussed. 
Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 Staff were observed using the kitchen handwashing sink adjacent to the dish area as a dump sink and a location for rinsing a wiping cloth. Proper use of handwashing sinks was discussed with all staff at the time of inspection. 
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing. Cease the practice of using handwashing sinks for other purposes.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11 Can opener blade was soiled with stuck on debris and was not used to open anything during prep for the current operating day. Kitchen manager took the can opener to the dish area to be cleaned and sanitized. 
Food contact surfaces shall be clean to sight and touch. Properly clean and sanitize food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils between uses.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 (A)(1) Some foods in the steam table were observed with internal temperatures below 135F and included mashed potatoes (117F), a portion of lasagna (97F-119F), and red sauce (124F). Other foods were observed with internal temperatures at 140F/above depending on when product was prepared and placed in the holding wells. Mashed potatoes were replaced with fresh product, which was observed with an internal temperature of 164F in the warmer. Lasagna was discarded as another portion of lasagna with an internal temperature of 143F was available for service. Red sauces were reheated to 165F prior to placing back in the steam table for service.
Water in the main holding well was observed at 170F, but products in the steam table were double panned. Double panning is not best practice if hot water is not adequate in the second pan to help maintain foods at 135F/above during hot holding. Kitchen manager stated he would change his process for hot holding at the steam table and monitor temperatures to verify best practice for hot holding.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control, cooked hot foods that require time/temperature control for safety shall be maintained at 135F/above.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17 (B) Open carton of whipping cream in the bar cooler was not date marked. Product was opened over the weekend on Saturday. Whipping cream was dated and kept for use. Whipping cream was also observed without a proper date mark at the bar during the previous routine inspection. Ensure proper date marks for all prepared TCS foods.
Refrigerated, ready to eat TCS food prepared and packaged by a food processing plant shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in ¶ (A). The day the original container is opened in the food establishment shall be counted as Day 1, and the day or date marked by the food establishment may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on food safety.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625  Sec. 3.06 Proof of food handler certification was not available for a server and front of house manager. Course was completed awhile ago and certificates need to be printed. Ensure all staff that are not certified food managers complete an online food handler certification course within 30 days of hiring, and maintain copies of certifications on-site.
All food handlers, other than someone who has a food manager certification, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 Sec. 3.07 Kitchen manager is currently the only person with a food manager certification and has not completed the food allergen awareness certification. Other members of the staff have the allergen certification but are not currently certified food managers. Management was advised as to the need for the certified food manager to complete the allergen course. Ensure the kitchen manager completes the food allergen certification by the next routine inspection.
Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Quat solution in cook line sani-bucket was observed at a concentration below 100ppm. Solution was prepared recently, and it appeared one of the tablets may have stuck to and possible dissolved into a wiping cloth. Additional tablets were added and brought the concentration to 200ppm
Sanitizer tablets were not dissolving in the server area sani-bucket due to the use of cold water to make the solution. Kitchen manager remade the solution with warm water, and the concentration was observed at 200ppm. 
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 (A)(1) Meat sauce and marinara in the warmer had internal temperatures of 121F and 111F. Kitchen manager noted the warmer was turned on around the same time the products were placed inside after being made fresh this afternoon. Alfredo sauce in the warmer had an internal temperate of 144F. All products in the warmer below 135F were reheated to 165F/above prior to placing back in the warmer for hot holding. Ensure hot holding equipment is on and at proper temperature to maintain hot foods at 135F/above prior to hot holding.  
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control, cooked hot foods that require time/temperature control for safety shall be maintained at 135F/above.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.18 (A) 1. Spinach dip and scampi butter in the walk-in cooler had prep dates of 12/20 and 12/16. Foods were discarded during inspection.
2. Open carton of whipping cream in the bar cooler was not date marked. Product was likely opened the evening prior. Whipping cream was dated and kept for use.
A food specified in ¶ 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in ¶ 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or package that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in ¶ 3501.17(A).

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.citation_text:
3-501.13 Thawed portions of vacuum packaged fish were observed in the kitchen reach-in cooler. Proper thawing of ROP fish was discussed. Packaging for thawed portions of fish was cut open during inspection. Ensure moving forward that packaging is cut prior to beginning thawing process for ROP fish. 
Reduced oxygen packaged fish that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment prior to its thawing under refrigeration as specified in ¶(A) of this section; or prior to, or Immediately upon completion of, its thawing using procedures specified in ¶ (B) of this section.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-302.13 Dish temp tester used to verify heat sanitization at the surface of dishes would not turn on. The battery was changed to allow for proper function of dish temp tester. 
In hot water mechanical warewashing operations, an irreversible registering temperature indicator shall be provided and readily accessible for measuring the utensil surface temperature. Surface temperature at dishes upon completion of final rinse must be at least 160F for proper heat sanitization.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 Cover was missing to a floor drain in the dish area. Replace the missing floor drain cover.
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 Floor along the wall under the dish machine was soiled with general buildup. Ensure floors are cleaned along the walls under/behind equipment as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.  
Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11 Can opener blade was soiled with stuck on debris. Can opener was taken to dish area to be cleaned and sanitized prior to use for dinner prep.
Food contact surfaces shall be clean to sight and touch. Properly clean and sanitize food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils between uses.
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 Black mold was beginning to accumulate on surfaces of the white baffle in the ice machine. Clean and sanitize inside the ice machine as needed to eliminate buildup.
Equipment such with enclosed components, such as ice makers, shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-302.13 Facility does not currently have an irreversible registering temperature indicator for checking the surface temperature at the dishes in the heat sanitizing dish machine. Owner ordered a dish temperature plate simulator during the inspection. Product should arrive by next week. 
In hot water mechanical warewashing operations, an irreversible registering temperature indicator shall be provided and readily accessible for measuring the utensil surface temperature. Surface temperature at dishes upon completion of final rinse must be at least 160F for proper heat sanitization.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12 Owner and all staff that were certified food managers still have not completed the food manager certification. Owner stated re-certification is scheduled to occur as of January. Additional information for locations to obtain certification, including an online process, were also provided.
Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food manager.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.citation_text:
2-401.11 Styrofoam cup of orange juice was observed in the server room on top of the coffee bean grinder. Drink was left by one of the staff from the previous operating day. Owner discussed proper storage of personal beverages with servers working at time of inspection, and drink in question was discarded. 
Food employees may drink from a closed beverage container if the container is handled to prevent contamination of the employee’s hands; the container; and exposed food; clean equipment, utensils, and linens; unwrapped single-service and single-use articles; or other items needing protection cannot result.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12 PIC was observed washing hands without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off without a barrier. Proper handwashing technique was discussed. 
To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.13 PIC was observed going between tasks without washing hands. A wet wiping cloth from a sani-bucket on the cook line was handled to wipe the food thermometer between temperature checks. PIC did not wash hands prior to touching mushrooms that were relocated between pans on the cook line. Handwashing between tasks was discussed, and PIC was observed washing hands between tasks the remainder of inspection.,
NOTE: Placing hands in and out of sanitizer solution does not count as having clean or sanitized hands to go directly to handling food, single service articles, or clean dishes. 
--PIC was also observed wiping his hands with a wet wiping cloth from sanitizer solution while walking around the kitchen. Proper use of wiping cloths was discussed. If hands need to be wiped, then they need to be properly washed. Cease the practice of wiping hands on wiping cloths.
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands must also be washed after doing anything with sanitizer or other chemicals and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11 Baked potatoes, soup, and meat sauce were observed uncovered in the walkin cooler. Shelving above food items had varying amounts of buildup (mold/general debris). PIC provided covers and noted the shelving was on the schedule to be cleaned today.
Food shall be protected from cross contamination by storing food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Final rinse concentration at the dish machine was observed at 0ppm chlorine. Chemical bucket was empty. Another 5gal bucket of sanitizer was not available and needed to be ordered. Regular bleach was available to connect to the dish machine until a new bucket is available. The final rinse concentration was observed at 100ppm upon connecting bleach to the machine. 
A chemical sanitizer shall be used in accordance with EPA-registered label use instructions. Maintain dish machine final rinse concentration as stated on the label instructions (no lower than 50ppm and no higher than 200ppm). Use test strips to verify concentration of bleach solutions.

findings.title: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding
findings.citation_text:
3-403.11 Mashed potatoes were observed heating in a warmer. Potatoes were placed in the warmer around 9:45am, and internal temperature was observed at ~78F around 10:30am. PIC was advised the warmer is not intended for rapid reheating to 165F/above w/in 2hrs. Mashed potatoes were moved to the stove to reheat rapidly prior to hot holding  (See General Comments).
TCS food that is cooked, cooled, and reheated for hot holding shall be reheated so that all parts of the food reach a temperature of at least 165F for 15 seconds and done rapidly to the time the food is between 41F and 165F may not exceed 2 hrs.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 Sec. 3.07 None of the staff that will be certified food managers have completed the online food allergen awareness training.
All certified food managers need to complete the food allergen awareness training by the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12 Owner and all staff that were certified food managers have expired certifications. Owner is working on getting himself and his staff re-certified (see general comments for details)
Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food manager.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12, 2-301.14, & 2-301.15 Bartender was observed rinsing hands at the prep sink by the salad cooler in the kitchen and then retrieving paper towels from the handsink by the walkin cooler to dry his hands. Bartender was advised to always use designated handsinks for handwashing and to properly wash hands when needed.
Owner wiped his hands on a dry wiping cloth between tasks while working on the cook line. Proper handwashing between tasks was discussed, and owner washed his hands at the handsink prior to continuing with preparation of a food order. 
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands must also be washed before putting on gloves/between glove changes and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.
Food employees shall clean their hands in a handwashing sink or approved automatic handwashing facility and may not clean their hands in a sink used for food prep, or warewashing, or in a service sink or a curbed cleaning facility used for the disposal of mop water and similar liquid waste.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 Back handsink adjacent to the dish area was used to prepare a sani-bucket. Owner was advised to cease using the handsink for any purpose other than handwashing. 
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114 Final rinse concentration at the dish machine was observed at 0ppm chlorine. Chemical bucket was changed, and several cycles ran to eventually show a final rinse concentration of 100ppm. 
A chemical sanitizer shall be used in accordance with EPA-registered label use instructions. Maintain dish machine final rinse concentration as stated on the label instructions (no lower than 50ppm and no higher than 200ppm). Use test strips to verify concentration of bleach solutions.
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 & 4-702.11 Can opener blade was soiled along the edge with buildup. Can opener was placed in dish area to go through ware washing.
Properly clean and sanitize food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils between uses and up to every 4hrs after continuous use for items such as the can opener. Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils shall be cleaned after use and sanitized before use after cleaning.

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.citation_text:
3-501.14 Pan of alfredo sauce in the walkin cooler prepared this morning at 10am was observed with an internal temperature of 48F after 4pm. Portion in question was discarded. A smaller portion of alfredo also prepared this morning and cooled was observed at 41F. Owner noted ice baths were used prior to placing pans in the walkin cooler. Parameters for proper cooling were discussed.
Cooked time/temperature control for safety food shall be cooled within 2 hours from 135F to 70F and within an additional 4 hours from 70F to 41F/below. Foods must be cooled in a total of 6 hours from 135F to 41F/below. 
Monitor the temperature of cooling foods with clean, calibrated stem thermometers to ensure foods are reaching bench mark temperatures in the designated time frames for proper cooling.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 Bowl of salad in the chiller was observed with surface temperatures of 46F-52F and internal temperatures of 50F-52F. Product was in use since 11am and was discarded.
Sliced tomato and cut leaf lettuce on the server line held in an ice bath had internal temperatures of 60F and 55F respectively. Only the bottom of the pan was in direct contact with the ice bath. Lettuce and tomato were discarded. Whipped butter packets in a pan at the same ice bath had internal temperatures of 41F for packets in the bottom of the pan and 84F for those in the top. Butter packets were discarded. A time control policy was established for these three items during the inspection today. 
Fettuccine in the 2 door cooler had an internal temperature of 48F-50F. Owner noted it was out for ~45 minutes during lunch service. Temperature was to be monitored and noodles discarded if they did not drop to 41F/below within the hour. 
Top portion of cooked vegetables in an ice bath on the cook line had an internal temperature of 53F, while the product lower in the pan was at 41F. Owner was advised on submersion of pans in ice baths and use of less product to help maintain colder temperatures. Top layer of vegetables were removed and discarded. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17 Cooked chicken and at least one pan of noodles in the 2 door cooler did not have date marks. Also, an open gallon of milk in the walkin cooler was without a date mark. Prep/open dates were provided. Ensure proper dates are indicated on all ready to eat, refrigerated foods that require date marking. 
Refrigerated, ready to eat, time/temperature control for safety food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature 41F/less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation and/or the original packaging is opened shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text:
7-102.11 A spray bottle at the bar labeled hard surface sanitizer was straight bleach (test strip bleached out when checked). Chemical was discarded by the owner. 
Working containers used for storing poisonous or toxic materials such as cleaners and sanitizers taken from bulk supplies and/or prepared on-site (bleach solution) shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.citation_text:
4-203.11 Food thermometer was checked in an ice bath and was observed reading below 30F. Thermometer was calibrated to 32F. 
Food temperature measuring devices that are scaled only in Fahrenheit shall be accurate to ±2°F in the intended range of use.  

4-204-112 Thermometers were not present in the 2 door cooler and the salad cooler. Provide functioning thermometers for all cold holding units used for storage of TCS foods. Thermometers were provided.
Cold or hot holding equipment used for time/temperature  control for safety (TCS) food shall be designed to include and shall be equipped with at least one permanently affixed temperature measuring device that is located to allow easy viewing of the device's temperature display.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11 Magnetic knife strip at the salad prep table was soiled with dust/crumbs along the top and general buildup on the magnetic strip. Clean the knife strip daily/as needed and maintain it clean. 
Clean utensils and equipment shall be stored in a clean, dry location, where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination.

findings.comment:
4-501.112 Heat sanitizing dish machine was not getting hot enough to allow for proper heat sanitization at the surface of dishes. After a half dozen plus cycles of the dish machine the wash gauge was reading around 140F and the rinse tank was below 160F. The Final rinse temperature gauge was reading above 180F, but the surface temperature at the dish rack in the machine was observed at 134F, 140F, and 135F using a dishtemp dishwashing tester. Manager stated another call for service would be made. (See general comments for additional details).
All dishes currently being washed and rinsed in the dish machine and then manually sanitized in quat solution until the dish machine is working properly.
The temperature of the fresh hot water sanitizing rinse as it enters the manifold may not be more than 194F or less than 180F for any dish machine that is not a stationary rack, single temperature tank.
findings.citation_text:

Equipment with enclosed components, such as ice machines, shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.citation_text:
4-301.11 Salad cooler was not holding foods at 41F/below. Shredded cheese just placed in the cooler after being held in the walkin cooler overnight was observed at 47F-49F. Inspector's stem thermometers were placed in the cooler to verify temperature and were later observed at 50F-51F. Cook noted the cooler was open so food could be iced down once the cheese was observed out of temperature. The cooler is holding at least in the high 40F range based on observations made. Kitchen manager stated a call for service will be made today to get the cooler repaired. Utilize ice baths to help hold foods at 41F/below until the cooler is repaired and able to maintain proper temperature. 
Equipment holding cold food shall be sufficient in number and capacity to maintain proper temperature of TCS foods.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.15 Owner rinsed his hands at the 3 part sink in the dish area. Owner was advised that if hands need to be rinsed or wiped then they need to be properly washed at a designated handsink regardless of the next task to be done. Owner was also advised to make sure employees working in the dish area are properly washing their hands at a designated handsink between handling dirty and clean dishes. 
Food employees shall clean their hands in a handwashing sink or approved automatic handwashing facility and may not clean their hands in a sink used for food prep, or warewashing, or in a service sink or a curbed cleaning facility used for the disposal of mop water and similar liquid waste

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11 Half of a small bread loaf was observed uncovered sitting on the top shelf in the reach-in cooler on the cook line. Cook noted it was likely left from only needing a portion for a half order the evening prior. Bread was discarded in the trash. 
Plate of baked potatoes was uncovered in the walkin cooler. Owner was advised to have staff cover foods after cooked foods are properly cooled. 
Food shall be protected from cross contamination by storing food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings and separating fruits and vegetables, before they are washed from ready to eat food.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.112 Heat sanitizing dish machine was not working properly. Wash temperature never went beyond 140F according to the gauge. The final rinse temperature was at 188F according to the rinse gauge, but Thermolabel heat strips verified the final rinse was not reaching 160F at the surface of the dishes. The heat strips did not turn black (4 separate strips were used at different times). A call for service was made. Until the dish machine is properly heat sanitizing, utensils and equipment need to be manually washed, rinsed, and sanitized. Dish machine may also be used for an initial wash prior to manual sanitization at the 3 part sink. 
The temperature of the fresh hot water sanitizing rinse as it enters the manifold may not be more than 194F or less than 180F for any dish machine that is not a stationary rack, single temperature machine.
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 Can opener had buildup along the edge of the blade and metal shavings in the crevice around the blade. Can opener was left soiled from previous use and not yet used during operations today. Can opener was taken to dish area to be cleaned and sanitized.
Surfaces of utensils and equipment contacting food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) shall be cleaned at any time when contamination may have occurred.
Equipment food contact surfaces and utensils used with time/temperature control for safety food shall be cleaned and sanitized throughout the day at least every 4 hours.

Stem of the food thermometer and the case had some stuck on food debris. Thermometer and case were cleaned during the inspection. Sanitizing between uses and manual wash, rinse, sanitize up to every 4 hours after continuous use were discussed. 
Food temperature measuring devices shall be cleaned before use or storage. 

Back surface of the baffle in the ice machine was soiled with mold accumulation. Owner noted the ice machine was cleaned and sanitized after the last inspection. Ice machine needs to be cleaned an sanitized as frequently as needed to eliminate buildup of mold. 
Equipment with enclosed components, such as ice machines, shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.citation_text:
3-501.14 Leftover foods from the previous evening were not properly cooled. Stacked pans of lasagna, manicotti, and sausage had internal temperatures of 50F-51F. The inner surfaces of the lids had condensation buildup on them. Also, a medium sized stainless steel pan full to the top with mashed potatoes had an internal temperature of 55F. All foods leftover from the previous evening were discarded. Proper cooling was discussed. 
Cooked TCS food shall be cooled within 2 hours from 135ºF to 70°F and within an additional 4 hours from 70°F to 41°F/below. Foods must be cooled in a total of 6 hours from 135ºF to 41°F/below. Utilize one or more of the following methods based on the type of food being cooled to allow for rapid/proper cooling: (1) Placing the food in shallow pans; (2) Separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) Using rapid cooling equipment; (4) Stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) Using containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) Adding ice as an ingredient; or (7) Other effective methods.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14 Damp wiping cloth was observed on the ledge of the steam table between uses. Wiping cloth was used to wipe the stem thermometer between temperature checks. Proper storage was discussed. Sani-buket was moved to the cook line to allow for proper storage of the wiping cloth between uses.
Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces shall be held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution maintained at proper concentration for the sanitizer product being used.

findings.title: Gloves used properly
findings.citation_text:
3-304.15 Cook was observed wearing a glove to prevent contamination from a bandaged finger. Glove was not being changed between touching unclean surfaces and using the oven mitt. Cook was also observed wiping his gloved hand on his apron. Proper glove use was discussed. Employee began changing his glove more frequently and washing hands between glove changes. 
Single use gloves shall be used for only one task, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-302.13 Facility does not have a way to check the temperature of the heat sanitizing dish machine other than the built in gauges. Owner was advised to purchase and use either dish machine heat strips or some type of maximum registering thermometer for monitoring and verifying the temperature to ensure proper function of the dish machine.
In hot water mechanical warewashing operations, an irreversible registering temperature indicator shall be provided and readily accessible for measuring the utensil surface temperature.
findings.citation_text:
4-302.14 Quat test kit was not available for checking sanitizer solutions. A chlorine test kit that had been purchased online was the only set of test strips available for use. Quat strips were purchased at a local restaurant supply store during the inspection and provided for use. 
A test kit that accurately measures the concentration of sanitizing solutions shall be provided.

findings.title: Hot and cold water available; adequate pressure
findings.citation_text:
5-103.12 Hot water was not available at the back handsink in the kitchen. This same handsink had issues with water pressure during the previous routine inspection. Owner noted a part had to be ordered a few weeks ago, and the whole faucet has to be replaced. 
Hot and cold water under pressure shall be provided to all fixtures, equipment, and nonfood equipment that are required to use water.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. Proof of a current food handler certification was not available for the cook or waitress working at the time of inspection. 
All staff that are not certified food managers need to complete an online food handler certification course that is ANSI and IL approved. Copies of certifications need to be maintained on-site.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment: PA 100-0367, Section 3.07 Certified food managers have not completed the online food allergen awareness training. Requirements for allergen training were discussed, and information was provided for management to find an online course. All certified food managers need to complete the food allergen awareness training by the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.120 & 250 - Cheese and dressing had internal temperatures of 49°F in the top holding area of the salad cooler. Air temp in the bottom of the cooler was around 45°F. Ice buildup on the condenser could have been causing an issue (see general comments). Salad cooler was just stocked this morning from products cold held in the walkin cooler, and the intention was to maintain foods at proper cold temperature when they were stocked. Manager was advised to use time control for the salad cooler until it could be properly defrosted. Foods would be served through lunch service and then replaced with fresh product.

Noodles, baked potatoes, and soup in the walkin cooler had internal temperatures of 47°F-50°F. Shell eggs had a surface temperature around 46°F. A huge delivery was received this morning and the cooler had to be stocked (see general comments). The air temp was blowing out below 40F. Kitchen Manager was advised to monitor temperatures to make sure they drop to 41°F/below. If products are questionable after lunch, then use or discard.

Cold foods shall be maintained at 41F/below at all times during storage, display, and service. .

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment:
750.510, 512, & 1120 - Cook was observed carrying a damp wiping cloth in his hands and wiping hands on the cloth after placing equipment in the dirty dish area. Cook stated the wiping cloth was not intended for his hands but was used to wipe down the counters. Wiping cloth was placed in the sanitizer solution on the cook line and hands were washed.

Member of the wait staff was observed putting on gloves and did not first wash her hands. Employee was advised on handwashing before putting on gloves.

Employees shall properly wash their hands any time hands may have been contaminated, prior to putting on gloves/between glove changes, and prior to working with food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles. 
Wiping cloths are not intended for use on hands. Cease the practice of wiping hands on damp or dry wiping cloths.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
(R) 750.650a - Push block on slicer was damaged with gashes along one end of the food contact surface. Owner stated a new part was ordered but had not yet arrived. Kitchen Manager stated it had been a few weeks since it was used. Food debris was obseerved on the blade and back side of the slicer. Owner stated the slicer would not be used again until the repalcement part arrives. The slicer was to be removed from the kitchen for the time being. 

Food contact surfaces shall be smooth, non absorbent, easily cleanable, and free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, pits, and free of difficult-to-clean internal corners and crevices.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - Sani-buckets in the kitchen were at 0ppm quat by the back handsink and ~100ppm quat on the cook line. Solutions were just prepared. More sanitizer was added to the solutions to bring concentrations to 200-400ppm.
Maintain sani-solutions prepared with the product in use at 150-400ppm quat as directed on label directions.

Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
(R) 750.800b - Mold buildup was observed on the back of the baffle in the ice machine. Owner stated a full cleaning will occur in early January. It is simply too busy right now to empty the ice machine for detail cleaning. In the meantime, the area in question will be wiped down with sanitizer. A barrier of baking sheets wil be used when surface is wiped, and a layer of ice will be removed/discarced once the process is done.

Clean and sanitize in the ice machine as needed to eliminate buildup of mold on all surfaces.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.citation_text:
750.1060 - Hot water had low pressure at the back kitchen handsink adjacent to the dish area. Kitchen Manager tried adjusting the pressure with the water line shut off, but it did not appear to be changing the pressure. Call a plumber for service.

All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.citation_text:
750.140 - Pan of mashed potatoes in the walkin cooler had surface and internal temperatures at 80°F and 82°F-92°F respectively. Product was on a roll cart and did not have any labeling. Kitchen Manager stated the product was just prepared prior to inspector's arrival and still within the first hour of the cooling process. Mashed potatoes were placed on an ice bath to speed up the cooling process.

Pan of marinara in the walkin cooler had surface and internal temperatures at 54°F. Kitchen Manager stated marinara is a canned product and was just opened around 2p to prepare for dinner service. Manager was advised to monitor the temperature and make sure marinara reaches 41°F/below by 6p.

TCS foods shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F. Monitor the time and temperature to ensure cooked foods are reaching bench mark temperatures in the designated time frame for proper cooling: 135°F to 70°F w/in 2hrs & 70°F to 41°F/below w/in an additional 4 hours. Foods prepared from ingredients starting at ambient temperature must reach 41°F/below w/in 4hrs.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.120 & 250 - Vegetable beef soup in the walkin cooler was observed with surface and internal temperatures at 50°F-51°F. Kitchen Manager noted the product was out for ~45 minutes at lunch time while product was removed to be reheated for hot holding. Container was placed on ice to help quickly drop the temperature.

Pan of vegetable soup on a roll cart was observed with surface and internal temperatures at 62°F-63°F. Kitchen Manager chose to discard the product.

Cold foods that require time/temperature control for safety (TCS) shall be maintained at 41°F/below at all times during storage, display and service. Be mindful that it doesn't take long for product temperatures to get in the danger zone above 41°F when out at ambient temperature. Promptly place foods back in coolers after retrieving the portion needed.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.citation_text:
750.130 - Raw fish products were stored below raw beef in the cook line reach-in cooler. BBQ sauce was also observed on the bottom shelf below raw meats. All foods were rearranged and placed in proper storage order with ready to eat foods on the top shelf above all other products and raw fish stored above raw meats.
 
All raw meat shall be properly stored, in the order of their cooking requirements with the lowest temperatures above all other meats and those with higher required cooking temperatures stored beneath.
All food shall be stored properly in order to prevent cross-contamination.  Store ready to eat foods above or away from raw foods.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
(R) 750.650a - Push block on slicer was damaged with gashes along one end of the food contact surface. Replace the push block.

Food contact surfaces shall be smooth, non absorbent, easily cleanable, and free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, pits, and free of difficult-to-clean internal corners and crevices.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - Sani-bucket on cook line was below 200ppm quat. Solution was remade at proper concentration of 200ppm.

Change solutions every 2 to 4hrs or more frequently if solutions and wiping cloths become heavily soiled. Maintain solutions at 200-400ppm quat as directed on label instructions.
Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750.800b - Mold was observed on the white baffle in the ice machine and on the left side wall. Ceiling inside behind the baffle was observed to be relatively free of mold, with the exception of one small section. Cleaning and sanitizing in the ice machine was discussed. 

Clean and sanitize inside the ice machine as frequently as needed to minimize the growth of mold.

findings.title: Hot food at proper temperatures
findings.comment:
(R) 750.120 0 & 250 - Cheese sauce on the steam table was observed at an internal temperature of 122°F. Cheese sauce was reheated prior to being place back on the steam table for service.

Hot foods that require time/temperature control for safety shall be maintained at 135°F/above at all times during storage, display and service.
NOTE: Use a clean, calibrated stem thermometer to check foods when they are being cooked and reheated. Verify reheated foods reach 165°F/above prior to placing on steam table for service.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.citation_text:
750.120 - Croutons and spinach bread on the top back ledge of the salad cooler were uncovered. Lids were placed on the pans during inspection.
Baked potatoes leftover from the evening prior were uncovered on plates in the walkin cooler. Potatoes were left uncovered to cool, which is fine. However, once products are cooled they need to be properly covered. Potatoes were covered.

Foods shall be properly stored and protected at all times. Cover foods during slow periods and after they have properly cooled to protect items from potential contamination.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
(R) 750.280 - Portion bowl was observed as a scoop in croutons. Portion bowl was removed. 

To avoid manual contact with ready to eat foods, proper utensils, such as scoops with handles, spoons, etc., shall be used for dispensing foods.
findings.citation_text:
750.290 - Metal ice scoop holders on ice bins were all observed with varying degrees of dust/general buildup. Clean and sanitize the ice scoop holders daily/as needed to eliminate buildup.

Ice scoop shall be stored on a clean surface or in the ice with the handle extended out of the ice

findings.title: Pre-flushed, scraped, soaked
findings.citation_text:
750.830 - Knife on magnetic strip had stuck on food debris (appeared to be from sliced lemons). Kitchen Manager placed knife in the dish area to be cleaned/sanitized.

Equipment and utensils shall be pre-flushed or pre-scraped and, when necessary, pre-soaked to remove gross food particles and soil prior to their being cleaned in a dishwashing machine unless a pre-wash cycle is a part of the dishwashing machine operation.
NOTE: If items are not clean when they come out of the dish machine, then repeat the ware washing process as many times as necessary to ensure removal of all food debris and soil.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.citation_text:
750.820 - A) Sanitizer solution in kitchen was observed at less than 200ppm quat. A wiping cloth was dipped in the solution prior to being used to wipe down the backside of the slicer. The solution was remade to be at 200ppm. The Kitchen Manager stated the slicer would be properly cleaned and sanitized before the next use.

Clean in place equipment must be properly washed, rinsed, and sanitized between uses.

B) (R) Sanitizer at bar 3 part sink was observed at ~100ppm quat. Solution was prepared earlier in the day. Old solution was emptied, and a new solution at proper concentration was provided (200ppm).

Equipment and utensils shall be sanitized in the third compartment according to one of the methods included in section 750.820 (e) (1) through (4).
Submerge items in sanitizer during manual ware washing for at least one minute prior to setting aside to air dry.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - Sani-bucket at the bar was observed at ~100ppm quat. A spay bottle labeled "Sani" that contained a light blue solution was at 0ppm quat. New solution was prepared in the sani-bucket at proper concentration(200ppm). Solution from spray bottle was discarded.

Maintain sani-bucket solutions at 200-400ppm quat. Change solutions every 2-4hrs or more frequently is wiping cloths and solutions become heavily soiled. 
Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750.800b - The following food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) (R) slicer (food debris on backside) - taken to dish area to go through ware washing; 
B) (R) soda gun nozzle/area where nozzle attaches (mold) - manually cleaned and sanitized at the bar during inspection;  and
C) inside ice machine - white baffle (mold).

Clean and sanitize food contact surfaces between uses/as needed, up to every 4hrs after continuous use, to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris.
Clean and sanitize inside the ice machine as needed to eliminate mold.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
(R) 750.1200 - Floor tiles under bar soda machine were damaged and holding moisture and debris. Clean and re-seal the tiles and areas where grout is low. This area could serve as a potential breeding location for pests.

Floors must be in good repair, constructed to facilitate easy cleaning, and maintained clean.
